used.how: WindowRing.put passes src itself when the piece is the whole tensor (a full-range ttnn.slice returns src's own buffer, which the dealloc after it would free)
full keeps the served 0_window_kv of every position as before; ring / none drop it from DS41ContractKV and the runner refuses them (tt-d-gen reads every position)
the ring keeps the bf16 rows the served cache keeps (the attention re-rounds the carry to bfp8 as from the slab), so ring and full read the same carry bytes
the region path's chip-0 carry stays the kept tail (rtail) for whole consecutive chunks; the ring is read only where full read the served slab (carry_ready / _kept mirror rtail_end)
a carry the ring does not keep is masked by truncation (start class 0, TtWindowCache.truncate), not by a zero carry
the rings are allocated with the state (load time) and written in place; the none working rings once per model (WindowTables.shared_ring)
test_window_ring's states take max_seq = a multiple of the chunk >= the follow-up's start + chunk (attempt 1 hit the compressor's history assert at 4000 + 2560 > 5120 with max_seq = the rung's 10240)
the ring's small copies (slice / slice_write / the own rows' untilize, <= 192 rows) run on one row of WINDOW_RING_CORES = 8 cores: plain profile wall 210.6 -> 206.4 ms (ring on)
replay128's decoder-tail windows are truncated by design; their window KV is recorded ungated (ring_diag_*), as P.31's owner note

missing: the frozen test_dram and the F230 position profiles run a chunk at start > 0 on a fresh state (the full path reads the never-written zeros): a keep mode that refuses missing carries has to treat a slot that never held a window row as starting there

overseer.evidence: nothing padded: the ring writes the chunk's own last 192 rows (32-row blocks, the record size), no op limit worked around
no Python-built op added or touched: the ring uses ttnn.slice / ttnn.concat / ttnn.to_layout / the slice_write fork (C++), the fabric all_gather it already used
no fork suite run; only the new model-level test_window_ring and the gate units
